title: Python SDK: typed output contracts & structured response helpers
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add first-class typed response models and helper utilities to the Python SDK to make structured output & streaming easier for application developers. Goals: (1) provide official pydantic (v2) model classes and optional dataclass adapters for responses and streaming events; (2) publish helpers to validate, coerce, and extract structured JSON output from model responses; (3) improve ergonomics for token/stream consumers when using typed models; (4) include examples and migration notes. This work reduces duplication in customer code, prevents silent schema drift, and makes downstream evals easier.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a `redwood.models` module with pydantic v2 BaseModel response classes for at least generation, chat message, and embedding responses
Optional dataclass conversion helpers documented and tested (dataclass <-> pydantic v2)
Structured output helpers: `safe_parse_json()`, `extract_schema_field()`, and `stream_to_model()` implemented and covered by unit tests
Streaming path supports incremental model population (partial fields allowed) and a stable API for async iteration over typed events
Examples folder contains 3 runnable examples: simple generation -> model, streaming tokens -> model assembly, and validation + retry flow
Performance regression < 5% for common synchronous call patterns compared to current untyped response path
Docs + migration guide added to Confluence and referenced in release notes
technical_decisions: Pydantic v2 chosen as primary typed model due to speed and V2's serialization API; dataclasses supported as opt-in convenience via helper adapters
Validation will be opt-in during streaming to avoid token latency penalties; `strict_validation` flag available for sync/verify flows
We will not add deep dependency to FastAPI or other frameworks; keep models framework-agnostic and small
For structured output helpers, use a conservative JSON-first parser that tolerates trailing tokens and common LLM artifacts (e.g., leading/trailing backticks)
Avoid mandatory runtime enforcement for existing customers by providing opt-in conversions and backwards-compatible return types
implementation_notes: Streaming API changes: add `response.iter_typed()` and `response.iter_tokens_typed(model=GenerationResponse)` as sugar methods
Unit tests under `tests/sdk/python/test_typed_models.py` covering edge cases: malformed JSON payloads, partial fields, incompatible types
Bench harness: run `bench/sdk_python_untyped_vs_typed.py` against a small local model to validate perf
Docs: Confluence page `SDK: Typed response models (Python)` and example notebook `examples/python/typed_models.ipynb`
